M15/M9 residue, 2026-08-05. Once lib-v1.5 made the fanout limit visible
to the tools, repair_design split all 22 over-fanout DATA nets by itself
and M9 fell from 5 to 1. What is left is ONE net at both limits:
clkbuf_0_clk/Y, fanout 16 vs 10 and cap 0.1157 vs 0.100 -- the top branch
net of the clock H-tree. It is not a data path and not a ring node.
TritonCTS was given -max_cap 5e-14 and still landed at 0.1157, because it
clusters on ESTIMATED wire and RCX then measured the real thing: ~81 fF of
the 116 is wire, only 34 is the 16 sinks' pin load. That gap is exactly
M12 -- the optimizer cannot see what signoff checks -- and M12's answer
was MARGIN, never a looser limit. So halve the budget CTS plans against.
A fast library makes hold OVERFIX expensive: default margins x a 171 ps
BUF_X2 produced 322 repair buffers = 27% of logic area and an infeasible
placement. 0.005 is the measured working value (stdcells, then harden/).
M12. Once lib-v1.4 gave STA real transition data instead of tables it
clamped to zero, post-route signoff found 58 max-slew violations at ss
(10 at tt, 0 at ff; worst 0.983 ns against set_max_transition 0.750).
They were always there -- M11 made them unreportable, so the old
'max slew violation count 0' was vacuous, not clean.
Repair had ALREADY run and succeeded: repair_design -slew_margin 20 at
32-openroad-repairdesignpostgpl found 24 slew violations and fixed them
with 50 buffers. It ran on ESTIMATED parasitics, before routing; the
real RC then put them back. The Classic flow has the step that would
catch that -- OpenROAD.RepairDesignPostGRT -- but librelane gates it on
this variable and its default is False, so it never ran (verified by
reading librelane 3.0.3 flows/classic.py:139 and :271, not guessed).
NOT enabling RUN_POST_GRT_RESIZER_TIMING: same family, but librelane
marks it experimental and prone to hangs, and setup slack is not the
problem here.
RISK, stated because this repo has been bitten by exactly it: this step
inserts buffers, and H3 was an insbuf pass that left a dangling buffer
on all 93 ring nodes -- corrupting the one number this die exists to
measure. tools/audit_netlist.py checks the ring stage counts on the
ROUTED netlist in CI, so that failure mode fails the build.
...and enabling it alone changed NOTHING (run 30933034059, netlist
byte-identical at 6953 devices). The step DID run and reported
'Found 1 slew violations', 0 resized, 0 buffers, area +0.0%. It was
not being lazy: at the view it can see there is genuinely nothing
wrong. Measured on the worst driver, _2566_/Y:
nom_tt <=0.750 (not a violator) | max_tt 0.760
nom_ss  0.935                   | max_ss 0.983
Repair runs on ONE estimated-parasitic view before extraction, and the
min/nom/max RC corners do not exist until RCX at step 54. So the
violations live in corners the optimizer structurally cannot see, and
no amount of pre-route repair will ever find them. PVT dominates (+29%
tt->ss), RC adds ~5% on top.
The fix is therefore MARGIN, not more repair passes: make the view the
optimizer CAN see land far enough under the limit that the corners it
cannot see still fit. Needed: 0.75 / 1.29 / 1.05 = 0.545 ns, i.e. ~27%
below the limit. 40% targets 0.45 ns and keeps a real cushion.
These percentages do NOT move the signoff limit (that is
MAX_TRANSITION_CONSTRAINT, still 0.75) -- they only tighten what repair
aims at, which is exactly the asymmetry the situation calls for.

CLOCK_PERIOD - Increase this in case you are getting setup time violations.
The value is in nanoseconds, so 20ns == 50MHz. Ship clock is 25 MHz; the
all-own build measured 10.5 ns of setup slack at this period.
If you need a custom clock configuration, read the following documentation first:
https://tinytapeout.com/faq/#how-can-i-map-an-additional-external-clock-to-one-of-the-gpios
SIGNOFF-ONLY SDC (READINESS.md M6). Gives STA the ring-oscillator
clock domain so the prescaler - an 8-bit counter clocked directly by
the ring at a predicted 914 MHz - is actually timed. Until 2026-08-02
there was no SDC at all and that counter had never been checked.

the H3 defect arriving by another road. See the header of the file.
